title: Comparing the surgical outcomes of femto laser-assisted cataract surgery (FLACS) versus conventional phacoemulsification (CP) in nanophthalmic eyes

license.statement: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 License); not CC BY or CC0, so the record is private

indication: Nanophthalmos (axial length 18.5-20.5 mm, RCS thickness at most 2 mm) with visually significant cataract (LOCS III up to NC2-NC4); all eyes primary angle-closure suspects treated with prophylactic Nd:YAG laser peripheral iridotomy 2 weeks before cataract surgery; pre-existing corneal or retinal pathology excluded

groups.description: Femtosecond laser-assisted cataract surgery (LenSx capsulotomy, lens fragmentation and corneal incisions, then phacoemulsification and in-the-bag IOL); randomized, one eye per patient, same surgeon
Conventional phacoemulsification (2.8 mm clear corneal incision, manual capsulorrhexis, direct chop, in-the-bag IOL); randomized, one eye per patient, same surgeon

series.baseline_label: Baseline = preoperative central ECD of the operated eye (Table 5 'Baseline'; Methods: ECL computed from the pre-operative central corneal ECD)
series.notes: Table 5 column 'FLACS (n=10)', rows 'Mean (SD) Min-max' under Baseline, 1 month and 3 months; the cell text starts with the mean. The row label unit '(mm)' is read as cells/mm2 (Methods). Per-visit n not tabulated.

series.baseline_label: Baseline = preoperative central ECD of the operated eye (Table 5 'Baseline'; Methods: ECL computed from the pre-operative central corneal ECD)
series.notes: Table 5 column 'CP (n=10)', rows 'Mean (SD) Min-max' under Baseline, 1 month and 3 months; the cell text starts with the mean. The row label unit '(mm)' is read as cells/mm2 (Methods). Per-visit n not tabulated.

Table 5 CDE and total surgery time rows

notes: Two established cataract techniques randomized against each other without an investigational agent; femtosecond-assisted surgery is listed under the protocol's cataract context, so both arms are control-role, separate groups.
All eyes had prophylactic Nd:YAG laser peripheral iridotomy 2 weeks before cataract surgery; the article does not state whether the baseline ECD was measured before or after the iridotomy.
Three CP patients developed refractory secondary glaucoma requiring additional surgery during follow-up (Results); no group was redefined.
